items.title: School founder said 5-year-old behaved 'suggestively', parent claims
items.description: Six women detail disturbing allegations of abuse and sexualised behaviour from the 1970s through the late 2000s at a controversial alternative school in Melbourne.

items.title: The vulnerable workers bearing the cost of providing Australia with cheap food
items.description: Behind the fruit and vegetables on Australia's supermarket shelves are workers whose stories are rarely heard.

items.title: Live: Minister tells Hanson to 'turn up and answer questions' after barring ABC, Guardian
items.description: Amanda Rishworth says Pauline Hanson must "turn up and answer questions" after the One Nation leader barred ABC and Guardian journalists from a press conference in Victoria. Follow live.

items.title: Older people open to downsizing but facing barriers
items.description: Research shows more than half of people over the age of 55 are open to downsizing. But experts say there are barriers stopping older people moving into smaller homes.

items.title: New vision shows moment airborne car hit Brisbane bus
items.description: New CCTV vision, captured from inside the bus, shows the moment the car ploughed into it, its front wheels coming to rest on a bus seat.

items.title: Infantino could face UEFA lawsuit as he scrambles for FIFA presidency support
items.description: European football body UEFA threatens FIFA with legal action over Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors.

items.title: Hens moved indoors but free-range label still allowed
items.description: The consumer watchdog has relaxed rules on free-range labelling as egg producers move their hens indoors to prevent the spread of bird flu.

items.title: Allegra Spender on the hardest decision she's ever made
items.description: Allegra Spender discusses her fashion mogul mother Carla Zampatti, the "joy" of politics and why no Liberal Party leader has ever tried to lure her into the fold.

items.title: 'Get this right': Top US Jewish leader's stark warning for Australia
items.description: The leader of one of the world's most high-profile Jewish organisations says Australia faces a crucial test on how it tackles the rise of antisemitism.

items.title: Ukraine drone strike on Russian holiday spot kills 11
items.description: At least 11 people are dead and dozens are wounded after Ukrainian strikes on a Russian beach resort and the Crimean Peninsula.

items.title: People living with disability gearing up for a fight as NDIS cuts loom
items.description: NDIS recipient Nicci Carlson, who is in constant pain and may soon lose her eyesight, says cuts to the scheme are making vulnerable people living with a disability scapegoats for Australians hit hard by cost-of-living pressures.

items.title: 'Nature doesn't follow your plans': Solo walker recounts rescue from Overland Track
items.description: An experienced Tasmanian hiker has told of her wilderness misadventure, not knowing if her emergency locator beacon was still working after plunging into icy water.

items.title: Australians warned prediction markets could cost them, with little protection
items.description: As Australians engage with billion-dollar prediction markets, betting on anything from war, weather to pop culture, the corporate watchdog is forced to step in.

items.title: Live: ASX opens higher as Wall Street rallies
items.description: The Aussie share market opens higher as Wall Street rallies. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: From Teardrop to Singapore ban, a guide to Massive Attack
items.description: Massive Attack have landed in Australia for a run of sold-out arena shows this week. If you're wondering what makes them such a big deal, here's your crash course.

items.title: Keen to invest but don't know where to start? Our expert breaks it down
items.description: If you've avoided investing because you've found the terminology intimidating, you're not alone. It can feel like a foreign language when you first start, but it's not as scary as it looks when you get into it.

items.title: How a father's love of music took his daughter to the world stage
items.description: From Newcastle in NSW to Windsor Castle in England, Christopher and Miriam Allan carry their family’s love of music across generations and continents.

items.title: Clues showing how breastmilk helps protect babies found by researchers
items.description: The international group of researchers found a breastmilk protein, osteopontin, triggers a cascade of biological processes that kickstart immune system development in early life.

items.title: Melbourne public hospital doctors to strike next week
items.description: Doctors at some of Melbourne's biggest public hospitals will walk off the job next week as part of a pay and conditions dispute with the state government.

items.title: Indonesians mock Trump-style 'personality politics'
items.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's repeated controversial comments spark debate over his "populist" communication style.

items.title: Myanmar releases rare images of ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi
items.description: Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi was visited by a delegate of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

items.title: Abortion clinic-style bans on protests outside WA places of worship unlikely
items.description: Bans on protesters congregating outside places of worship are unlikely to be introduced in WA, despite suggestions from senior Jewish legal figures amid heightened antisemitism.

items.title: Blues announce King as new Origin coach after Daley steps down
items.description: Former NSW State of Origin player Matt King has been named the new head coach of the Blues.

items.title: With a new heart, 18-month-old Noah is finally coming home
items.description: The Forster family is set to make an emotional journey home to WA after their infant son Noah received a life-saving heart transplant.

items.title: Almost $140m in fines written off by Queensland government
items.description: More than 460,000 debts were written off by the state government last financial year, almost double the amount written off two years ago.
